questions.prompt: Which empire did Justinian I rule?
questions.fact: His legal code was rediscovered in medieval Italy and became the foundation of law across much of continental Europe.

questions.prompt: What is the term for the splitting of an atomic nucleus?
questions.fact: It was discovered by accident in 1938, and the physicist who explained it was excluded from the Nobel that followed.

questions.prompt: Which country won the first Cricket World Cup in 1975?
questions.fact: They won the next one too, and the final in 1975 finished close to nine in the evening in midsummer London.

questions.prompt: Which musician recorded the album Blue?
questions.fact: She used unconventional guitar tunings extensively, partly because polio in childhood limited her left hand.

questions.prompt: Which country contains the source of the Amazon river?
questions.fact: The exact source was disputed for centuries and was only settled in the 1970s by satellite survey.

questions.prompt: Who wrote the novel A Clockwork Orange?
questions.fact: He invented an entire slang for it, drawn largely from Russian, so the book would not date.

questions.prompt: Which company manufactures the M-series chips used in Macs?
questions.fact: They put processor and memory on the same package, which is much of why they run so cool for their speed.
